title: QUIC RFC 9000 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED Send-Only Receive Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded receiver-side policy that closes the connection when a protected STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame targets a send-only stream.
design_summary: The protected Application Data frame loop delegates STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED receive-policy validation to QuicConnectionStreamState.TryReceiveStreamDataBlockedFrame. That seam accepts receive-capable peer streams and returns STREAM_STATE_ERROR for send-only local unidirectional stream IDs. The runtime now preserves that transport error by converting the failed STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED receive-policy check into a local CONNECTION_CLOSE transition with triggering frame type 0x15.
data_and_state_considerations: This slice does not change STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED parsing, formatting, sender-side advisory emission, or stream flow-control credit accounting. It only ensures the existing receive-capability check is surfaced as a connection close when the offending frame arrives on a protected runtime packet path.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Receive-capable bidirectional streams remain accepted and do not close the connection.
Opened locally initiated unidirectional streams are send-only for this endpoint and close with STREAM_STATE_ERROR when targeted by STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED.
Uncreated locally initiated unidirectional stream IDs are also send-only by stream-ID direction and close with STREAM_STATE_ERROR.
The local close records STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame type 0x15 as the triggering frame type.
alternatives_considered: Leave the bookkeeping seam proof as sufficient; rejected because the RFC requirement says the endpoint must terminate the connection, which requires protected runtime close behavior.
Fold this into the S19P13 frame-shape proof; rejected because ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0052 intentionally covers parser and field-boundary behavior only.
Add new STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED parser behavior; rejected because the parser and formatter were already closed for requirements 0003 through 0008.
risks: This proof remains limited to the current protected Application Data runtime path.
This proof does not claim new STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED emission scheduling, flow-control autotuning, or sender/recovery behavior.
Malformed STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED field encodings remain parser/formatter proof under ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0052 rather than this receive-policy slice.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers only REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-1299 receiver-side termination for STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames that target send-only streams.
